$schema.description: Path or URL of imeng.schema.json (editor help only).

schema_version.description: Version of this file's format. Missing means 1.

description.description: One or two sentences on what this imeng is and does (shown when someone asks what it is).

model_id.description: Name shown in Open WebUI's model list.

icon.description: An image file in the game folder (png, jpg, webp or gif, up to 2 MB) used as the game's picture. The server serves it at /icons/<model_id> (base: PUBLIC_URL) and logs that address at start. Open WebUI's model editor takes an uploaded file, not an address: upload this file in Workspace > Models. Off when absent.

history_limit.description: Old name of actor_history_limit (v1.1). Still accepted.

actor_history_limit.description: Default 20. Max entries kept in each actor's history list.

private_guidance.description: How the actors of this game use the private channel (<private>, private chats), in words. Told to the judge that decides who a private message is for and to the narrator when a private part is present. Example: "Contestants whisper to each other or to the Host; a note to the Host is for the Host alone."

private_only_reply.description: Default "...". What the player sees when the narrator's whole reply was inside <private>...</private> (which the player never sees; env SHOW_PRIVATE=1 shows it while debugging). Example: "The Host makes notes.". Game.json only: not a state field, so no model can change it.

too_long_reply.description: What the player is told (HTTP 413) when a message makes the prompt too big for the hardware (env CONTEXT_MAX_TOKENS). Nothing is saved; they edit and resend. Default: a plain English line.

exit_when.description: Auto-exit an actor when the condition holds: a comparison on one field, or an AND/OR/NOT tree with aggregates (avg/min/max/sum over actors still in).

exit_group_when.description: End the game for everyone when the condition holds: like exit_when, but a plain comparison needs `share` of the actors still in.

field_evidence.description: An actor field that changes only when the narrator's own words contain a phrase: {"score":"point to {name}"} (a case-insensitive regular expression; {name} is the actor's name, address_as or id). What the player says never counts, and a change the narration does not support is dropped, not retried.

actor_ref_fields.description: Fields that hold an actor id, besides game.current_actor: "game.<field>" for a shared field, a bare name for a field of every actor. Writes are checked (an id, or a name the judge model matches) and the field is cleared when that actor leaves. Server-owned and nested entries are ignored.

id_domains.description: Places where things with ids live ("actors" always is one). A new entry is made with the add op, removed with drop.

key.description: Set it when the container is an array of objects: the field of each entry that holds its id. Leave it out for a map (the key is the id).

from.description: The field the natural id comes from, and the default input of a hash or a uuid 5. Default name.

when.description: creation (default): mint an id for every new entry. collision: use the natural id (the name, as a slug) and mint only if it is taken. change: mint at creation and again whenever `from` changes (every reference follows).

mint.description: How a new id is made. Leave it out: the id is the one given, or the slug of `from`, and a taken id is refused.

version.description: 4 random (default), 5 from a field (same name, same id), 7 time-ordered.

namespace.description: uuid 5: the namespace UUID (default: the DNS namespace).

of.description: uuid 5: the field it is made from (default: `from`).

alphabet.description: digits, hex, base32, base36, base58, base62 (default), base64url, or the characters to use.

format.description: Default epoch_ms. iso uses - instead of : and . so it is a valid id.

of.description: The field it is made from (default: `from`).

refs.description: Fields that must hold ids of a domain: {"game.location":{"to":"locations"},"actors.*.inventory":{"to":"items"},"actors.*.counts":{"keys_to":"items"}}. A write is checked (an id, or a name the judge model matches); the field is cleared when the entry goes.

repeat.description: Arrays: may the same id appear twice? Default false.

multiplayer.description: Shared games. Off unless enabled is true.

enabled.description: Default false. Several real people play one game: a chat shared with Open WebUI's "Allow replies" (or a channel) is the table.

turns.description: How a round starts. ready (default): collect what everybody says, narrate when all said ready. free: every message is a round. token: only the holder of token_field acts. judged: the judge model decides from turn_rule.

token_field.description: Policy token: the game field that names the actor whose turn it is. Default game.current_actor.

off_turn.description: Policy token or judged: what happens to a message that is not its author's moment. note (default): they are told; queue: it is kept and goes in with the next round.

turn_rule.description: Policy judged (and context for the judge in any policy): the rule in words, e.g. "Only the crane operator reacts to radio calls; the foreman may speak at any time."

order.description: How several players' lines in one round are sequenced: fifo (arrival, default), filo (latest first), join (the order people joined), random, or by an actor field such as initiative.

clock.description: The in-game clock that in-game timeouts and away-time use.

unit.description: What one step of the field is. count (default) is a plain counter such as a round number.

tension.description: Tension beats while the table waits.

mode.description: What the table sees while the game waits on someone. status (default): a terse line ("Ready: Bea. Waiting for: Bo."). beats: the narrator writes one short in-story line that keeps the waiting player's declared action in suspension (an extra short narrator call per message).

cooldown_seconds.description: Default 0. Minimum time between two beats; in between, the terse status is used.

private.description: A seated player's new chat with the game is a private channel to the narrator. false turns private chats off.

reply.description: What a player gets in their private chat. ack (default): a short fixed line. narrator: a short private narrator reply (an extra narrator call). none: "(noted)".

unseated.description: Default ignore. A <private>-only message in the shared chat from someone who is not at the table: ignore answers with private_only_reply and keeps nothing; seat puts them at the table (as if they had spoken) and files the note.

forget.description: Default false. true: the private notes of a round are not kept in the table transcript once the round is narrated (the narrator is told them for that round only). Anything that must outlast it belongs in the state, a standing instruction or a goal, never in the transcript.

narrator_sees.description: Default true: private notes go to the narrator with the next round, marked never to reveal.

silenced_when.description: A condition on a player's own character, e.g. {"field":"hp","lte":0}. A person whose character meets it is ignored in the shared chat (no state change, no narrator call; they get silenced_reply); their private channel still works. For the dead.

silenced_reply.description: Default "The living do not hear you."

seat_days.description: Default 14. How long a seat at a table keeps a person's new chats private.

leave_pattern.description: Regular expression (case-insensitive) a whole message must match to leave the table. Default: "leave the table" / "quit the game".

standing.description: Where "if I do not answer in 5 days, assume ..." instructions are accepted from: private chats only (default) or any chat.

default_after.description: How long the game waits on a player who left no standing instruction before default_action happens. Omit to wait forever.

real_from.description: A game field holding a duration (e.g. imeng.idle_after): when it parses it replaces `real`, so a table can agree its own limit. Only the next message from anyone else applies it; the person being waited on acts normally, however late.

game.description: In-game time, in the clock's unit (or a duration when the clock has a time unit).

idle_vote.description: /idle: once someone has held the table up longer than the registered limit, the other players can vote to move them on (their default action, and they sit out until they speak). Needs more than half the others.

limit.description: State path holding the idle limit the table agreed at registration, as a duration like "3m" (default imeng.idle_after).

min_votes.description: The fewest votes that can move a blocker on (default 2; never more than the other players).

default_action.description: What that player's character does then. Default "says nothing".

judge.description: Default true: the judge model reads messages at a table of two or more (turn rule, stepping away, standing instructions). false: code only.

gate.description: Old name: false means turns free.

confirm_pattern.description: Policy ready: regular expression (case-insensitive) a whole message must match to count as ready. Default: ready, confirm, confirmed, done or go.

reset_on_talk.description: Policy ready: default true. Saying something new after "ready" takes the ready back.

min_players.description: Default 2. The turn policy only applies once this many people are at the table; with fewer, every message is a round.

idle_minutes.description: Default 0 (wait for everyone). Players quiet for longer than this are not waited for.

knowledge.description: Secrets and partial knowledge. Off unless enabled is true; needs multiplayer.

enabled.description: Default false. Facts only some people know (a goal, a hidden trait, something only some of them saw). Needs multiplayer: players record them in their private chat.

confirm_facts.description: player (default): the player confirms a fact the judge structured before it is saved. off: it is saved at once.

match.description: How the server decides a knower speaks or is addressed this round. name (default): their name or actor id appears in the round. judge: the judge model reads the round (never sees the fact).

action.description: Default none: an action trigger reveals the fact when the judge sees it (and the quote checks out). owner: the person it is about must confirm.

statement.description: Default owner: a statement trigger waits for the person it is about to confirm in their own next lines. none: it reveals at once. A fact about an NPC cannot be confirmed by anyone and reveals at once.

candidate_turns.description: Default 3. How many rounds a seen statement waits for confirmation.

leak.description: The narrator can state a fact in a reply the whole table reads. retry (default): the reply is held (not streamed) when a fact was given to the narrator this round, scanned, rewritten once on a hit, then redacted. redact: scanned and redacted. audit: scanned after delivery and logged. off: no scan.

notice.description: Default seen: when something is passed on in secret (a whisper, a look, a note), the narrator is told on the next round that the table saw it happen, never what it was, so it can narrate it. off: nothing is said.

covert_with.description: Which model writes the NPCs' secret dealings each round (transfer covert). judge (default): the small judge model, off the GPU; main: the narrator model. Code keeps only what names real NPCs and fits the limits either way.

debrief.description: Needs transfer. When a listed phase is entered, the producer asks every real player privately what they gathered from the secrets that passed since the last debrief (they answer in their private chat or with /goal), and the narrator is told what each NPC witness gathered. The producer never writes what anyone knows. Off when absent.

phases.description: Phases that start a debrief when entered (default [crossing]): the same beats as the ambient updates.

ask.description: What each real player is asked privately. {what} lists what passed.

report.description: What the narrator is told about the NPCs' gathering. {npc} lists it.

overhear.description: Needs transfer. Every other NPC who witnesses a whisper always knows that one happened (the narrator is told), never what was said; whether it catches the content is a dice roll by code from these traits. Off when absent.

traits.description: roll (default): when an NPC joins, the server rolls its nosy_field and respect_field once, uniformly from 0 to 1, so every game starts every NPC from the same fair baseline (the narrator does not pick them). none: the game sets them itself.

text.description: What a real player who catches a fragment is told, privately. {who} is who dealt with whom, {what} the fragment.

base.description: Chance (default 0.2) that an NPC who witnesses a secret dealing catches its content.

step.description: How much each point of nosiness over respect adds to the chance, and the extra for an NPC that moves closer (default 0.3).

seek.description: Nosiness at or above which an NPC moves closer on purpose (default 0.7).

nosy_field.description: Actor number field 0 to 1 (default nosiness): how much it wants to hear everything.

respect_field.description: Actor number field 0 to 1 (default respects_privacy): how much it leaves others' secrets alone.

transfer.description: Default off. tell: a player can pass a fact on to named characters in their private chat (a whisper, a signal, a look); only the recipients then know it. covert: tell, and after each round the model lists what NPCs secretly pass to each other (one extra model call per round; needs two or more NPCs).

covert_max.description: Default 2. Most covert acts recorded per round.

notes_view.description: Default true: a player can list and forget their own facts in their private chat.

max_chars.description: Default 1500. Most characters of facts put in one narrator prompt.

audit_keep.description: Default 200. Audit entries kept (ids and turns, never the text).

confirm_pattern.description: Whole message that confirms a pending fact. Default yes/y/save/confirm/ok.

cancel_pattern.description: Whole message that drops a pending fact. Default no/n/cancel/discard.

notes_pattern.description: Whole message that lists the player's own facts. Default notes/secrets.

forget_pattern.description: Message `forget <id>` that removes the player's own fact (first group is the id). Default forget <id>.

seed.description: Facts the game itself holds (an NPC's agenda, a role's goal).

known_by.description: Actor ids or names of who in the story knows it.

access.description: never: no model sees it until revealed. roleplaying: given to the narrator only when a knower speaks or is addressed. dm: kept as a note, never given to a model. Default roleplaying when known_by is set, else never.

discord.description: How the Discord interface treats this game (modules/discord, docs/DISCORD.md). The proxy itself ignores it.

scope.description: Who shares a conversation with the bot. user (default): every person has their own 1:1 conversation with it, even in a public channel. channel: the channel is one shared conversation (a table).

merge_context.description: Background the bridge adds when a message points at other messages. mentions (default): the message being replied to, and the latest exchanges the bot had with people the message mentions. reply: only the message being replied to. off: none.

history_limit.description: Default 200. How many channel messages the bridge reads to rebuild a conversation.

sync.description: Keeping the record in step with the conversation. The conversation is the truth; the saved state is a cache derived from it.

mode.description: Default detect: remember a fingerprint of each turn and keep an audit log, but repair nothing. repair: when the conversation no longer matches the record (an earlier message was edited, turns were missed, or the record is gone), roll back and replay the turns through the extractor. off: neither.

replay_turns.description: Default 10. At most this many of the latest turns are replayed when the record is rebuilt; older ones keep the state before them.

batch.description: Default 4. Turns per extractor call when replaying.

similarity.description: Default 0.7. How much of a reply must still match its saved fingerprint (0 to 1) for an edited reply not to count as a change.

audit_keep.description: Default 200. Audit log entries kept with the session.

tools.description: Tools the narrator may call, each with its options: {"tmdb":{"max_calls_per_turn":4},"fetch":{"hosts":["api.example.com"]}}. Every tool takes max_calls_per_turn (3), max_chars (6000) and timeout_ms (15000). Built in: fetch, web_search, tmdb, stock, poker (hand ranking and pot settlement; options variant, leave_rule, borrow_limit). Keys and endpoints go in tools.config.mjs, never here.

tool_rounds.description: Default 3. How many model-and-tool rounds one turn may take.

field_access.description: Per field ("game.<field>" or an actor field): "normal" (default, same as not listed or null), "read-only" (ops cannot write it; its value can still be copied with an address) or "write-only" (ops can write it by path; its address can never be used in a value). A key covers what is inside the field and what contains it.

while.description: Condition on another field; leave out to lock the field for good (it can never go down).

early_sync.description: Record what the player's message states while the narrator is still writing (one more extractor call per turn). Default false.

game_turn.description: Game turns, separate from the chat round. The count is game.game_turn in the state (server-owned, rolled back with the state). Needs nothing else; default off.

advance.description: Default round: every chat round is a game turn. field: a game turn passes when the numeric game field in `field` goes up. judged: the judge reads each round (public and private) and decides from `rule` whether a game turn has completed; it may also release a timed effect that ended in the story.

field.description: advance field: the game field to watch, "game.<name>".

rule.description: advance judged: when a game turn completes, in words. Example: "One show round is the questions to every contestant and then Punishment Time; it completes when the Host has handed out the last punishment."

word.description: What this game calls a game turn: turn (default), round, segment, quarter, game, match, or any short word. Used in what the narrator is told.

link.description: Link one person's accounts (Open WebUI and Discord) so the game sees one player: /link prints a code, /link <code> in the other app joins them. Off unless this block exists.

length.description: Characters in a link code (default 8). Letters O, I and L and the digits 0 and 1 are never used.

style.description: chars (default): random letters and digits. words: three words from `words`, easier to remember.

words.description: The word list for style words (at least 16 words, no hyphens).

ttl.description: How long a code works (default "10m"). Codes live only in memory: a restart or the clock loses them.

max_fails.description: Wrong codes one person may try within the ttl (default 5).

texts.description: Wording: code, dm_sent, linked, already, bad_code, locked, none_to_link. {code}, {minutes} and {name} are filled in.

rehydrate.description: Keeps the listed values in the database between sessions and puts them back when the person returns or something outside the game changes them. Needs DATABASE_URL.

paths.description: Per-person paths kept in SQL, only as actors.*.<field> (* = the person's own actor): numbers, booleans, enums and ids, never free text. e.g. ["actors.*.chips","actors.*.credit"].

ttl.description: How long a stored value is kept without being seen (default "30d").

notes.description: "Since you slept" lines by path, for a value something else changed: {"actors.*.credit":"{name} now has {value} credit (was {old})."}.

eligibility.description: Who may join: named flags kept per person in the database (needs DATABASE_URL). Off unless this block exists.

version.description: Bump when a flag is renamed or removed (the stored masks are then reset by db:migrate). New flags go at the end.

join.description: Joining a table needs every require flag and no block flag.

rules.description: After each turn, a flag is on while path (actors.*.<field>) satisfies the condition; with latch it stays on.

texts.description: Wording: cannot_join {missing}, missing {list}, blocked {list}, opted_in, opted_out, no_opt, no_db.

crossings.description: Moving between two places with a server-rolled ambient effect, and an optional one-time ad break. The reply stops at each crossing. Off unless this block exists.

phase.description: The phase the game sits in between the reply that sends everyone across and the player's next message.

back.description: The phase play returns to once the crossing is done.

places.description: Exactly two places; each crossing goes to the other one.

ambient.description: The field holding the weather or mood (default "game.ambient").

effects.description: Per ambient value, per actor field, [lowest, highest] change rolled by the server for every active actor.

text.description: What the narrator is told to do: an in-story interruption, then carry on as if it never happened.

at_crossing.description: Which crossing carries it (default 2). Once per game; nobody is affected by the ambient on that crossing.

pii_filter.description: Keeps personal details out of every model, log and trace, in code, at the door. Set env PII_SALT so the tokens cannot be guessed. Off unless this block exists.

detect.description: Kinds to look for (default all): email, phone, card (Luhn-checked), id_number (SSN, SIN, IBAN), ip, secret (a password or token in a URL or key=value).

on_detect.description: mask (default): the value becomes a token like [email:3fa9c2] before any model, log or trace sees it. block: the message is refused with texts.blocked and read by nobody. allow: only counted in the log.

allow.description: Exact values that are fine to keep, e.g. a support address that appears in your own text.

patterns.description: Game-specific patterns: name (a-z, 0-9, _) becomes the token's kind.

names.description: Also find people's names, family and role words, animals and sensitive facts (religion, health, politics, orientation) with the small local judge model, and mask them (default false). If the judge cannot be reached the message is refused (texts.detector_failed) and a review line is logged.

new_class_judge.description: Default false. A second judge call per message finds private data the classes do not name (a PIN, an address, an employer, a licence plate). It is masked as [other:...], only its label is logged, and the whole message is refused if this call fails. Needs names.

classes.description: Which name classes are masked (default all three): person (a name, keeping the relation or role beside it: [uncle:3fa9c2]), animal (named pets and livestock), sensitive (the whole phrase).

mappings.description: How what the detector found becomes a class. Built in: person to person, animal to animal, health/religion/politics/orientation to sensitive, role and relation to person or sensitive (the judge decides). Yours replace the built-in one with the same `from`.

from.description: What the detector calls it: person, animal, role, relation, health, religion, politics, orientation, or your own word.

to.description: Classes it may become, least protective first. One entry decides it; several are decided by the judge (the most protective, the last, if the judge fails). keep leaves it clear.

judge.description: The question the judge answers for this mapping (it replies with one of the `to` words).

restore.description: Show the player the real names again in the narrator's reply (default true). Secrets (passwords, PINs) are never restored.

placeholders.description: Fixed text for a kind instead of a hashed token, for values that must never be recoverable (a hash of a 4-digit PIN can be guessed). Default: {"secret": "[SECRET]"}. Add your own pattern name, e.g. {"pin": "[PIN]"}.

pii.description: Paths of personal data, e.g. ["actors.*.real_name","game.contact"] (`*` = one key). Masked before it reaches SQL, logs or MLflow; a stored (rehydrated) path may not be listed here.

pii_mask.description: What a personal value is replaced with (default "[redacted]").

state.description: The bookkeeping database (env DATABASE_URL). Its wording.

texts.description: Wording: unavailable (the reply while the database's version stamp is wrong).

owner.description: The chat has an owner (whoever starts it), who names successors and controls /telemetry. Ownership passes only through /claim after the owner has been away. Off unless this block exists.

vanish_after.description: How long the owner can be away before the chat may pass on (default "7d").

fallback.description: No successor is around: close (default) the chat, or open it to anyone who answers the claim questions.

answers.description: How the claim answers are kept in the saved chat: hashed (default) or plain.

challenge.description: Questions a claimant must answer, in order: created (the day the chat began), name (the first owner's name). Default both.

tone.description: Successors must opt in (/successor accept) and be rated kind and level-headed by a small judge. Only the number is kept. Off unless this block exists.

min.description: The lowest tone score (0 to 1) a person may have and still be named or suggested as a successor (default 0.5).

every.description: Spoken turns between asking a person if they want to be considered, and between ratings (default 15).

ask_after.description: How often the owner is asked whether to keep the room (/keep) or hand it over (/handover <name>), with suggested successors scored from activity, recency and tone (default "7d").

max_fails.description: Wrong answers before a claimant is locked out until the owner returns (default 3).

texts.description: Wording of every reply (owner, no_owner, not_owner, successor_added, ...).

telemetry.description: What players are told about telemetry.

notice.description: always (default): when MLflow is on, the first reply says so, and so does any later change. never: say nothing.

freeze.description: Freeze and unfreeze a character (someone is in the bathroom, or went to another app). Off unless this block exists. Frozen players are skipped by the turn policy of a multiplayer table.

mode.description: What a frozen character is. skip (default): the table does not wait for them and the narrator leaves them out. npc: the narrator plays them as an NPC. inert: present in the scene but silent and still.

catch_up.description: What a returning person learns. none (default): nothing is shown and the character does not know what happened. public: they are shown the narration since they froze (never whispers or private notes) and their character knows it.

catch_up_chars.description: Most characters of narration shown on return (default 1500, the newest).

others.description: off (default): people freeze only themselves. anyone: /freeze <name> and /unfreeze <name> work on any character, players and NPCs.

text.description: What the narrator is told about a frozen character ({who} is their name). Default depends on mode.

texts.description: Wording: frozen, unfrozen, you_are_frozen, nobody, not_allowed, unknown_who, solo, not_frozen, catch_up. {who} and {story} are filled in.

images.description: Image generation from the chat (/draw, /portrait, /keepsake). Off unless this block exists.

renderer.description: Which image backend to call. comfyui: an API-format workflow file (seeds and reference images). a1111: AUTOMATIC1111/Forge txt2img and img2img (seeds, negative prompt, reference). openai: any /v1/images/generations server such as Open WebUI's image engine (no seed). ollama: Ollama's experimental image models through the same endpoint (no seed; macOS first).

url.description: Base URL of the renderer. The env IMAGE_URL overrides it. Defaults: comfyui http://127.0.0.1:8188, a1111 http://127.0.0.1:7860, openai http://127.0.0.1:8080, ollama http://127.0.0.1:11434.

workflow.description: comfyui: path (in the game folder) of a workflow exported with Save (API Format). Placeholders ${positive} ${negative} ${seed} ${width} ${height} ${steps} are filled in; a string that is exactly one placeholder keeps its number type.

workflow_reference.description: comfyui: the workflow used when a reference image exists (img2img or IP-Adapter). It may also use ${reference}, the name of the uploaded image. Without it a reference is ignored.

model.description: a1111: checkpoint name; openai/ollama: model name.

strength.description: a1111 img2img denoising strength when a reference is used (default 0.6).

prompts.description: Fixed prompt parts. Every render is style + the scene the judge writes + positive; negative is sent as is.

seeds.description: Seeds by actor id or name. An actor with no entry gets a random seed the first time it is drawn, and keeps it for the session.

reference.description: default: a file in the game folder (or, with urls, an http(s) URL) used as the reference for every render. urls: allow players to pass a URL (default false). Only PNG, JPEG and WebP are used; SVG, PDF and anything else is refused.

ask.description: Let the judge notice a player asking for a picture and offer one (the player must still answer yes). words: only messages containing one of these are looked at (default: every message). offer: how the offer begins (default 'Make an image of').

process.description: A program the engine starts when it is not already answering (ready_url, default the renderer url). ${NAME} in command, args, env values and cwd is replaced from the engine's environment; a name that is not set stops the start. It is left running when the engine exits unless stop_on_exit is true.

venv.description: A Python virtual environment folder (${NAME} allowed). The program runs as if it were activated (VIRTUAL_ENV, its bin first on PATH; a bare python/pip is the venv's own). Implies stop_on_exit unless set to false.

stop_on_exit.description: Stop the program (and what it started) when this app is stopped. Default false, or true when venv is set.

lease.description: Around a render the narrator model is unloaded from Ollama (keep_alive 0) and narrator calls wait; afterwards the renderer frees its VRAM. Both default true.

max_queue.description: Renders waiting behind the running one before new requests are refused (default 3).

texts.description: Wording of the server's replies: busy, queue_full, failed, bad_format, unsafe, safety_down, unknown_who, no_game, caption, offer_confirm, keepsake_not_over, keepsake_not_you, keepsake_claimed, keepsake_pick, keepsake_hint, keepsake_bad, keepsake_none. {who} and {subject} are filled in.

judge.description: A different judge model for the picture prompt and the offer (env IMAGES_JUDGE_MODEL / _URL / _API win).

state_fields.description: Actor fields the prompt writer is given for every actor (e.g. description, outfit, gak_colors).

game_fields.description: Game fields (game.<name>) the prompt writer is given for the scene.

keep_fields.description: Actor fields whose values must appear in that actor's picture prompt: code adds any the judges left out.

refine.description: A second pass that rewrites the prompt for a renderer that understands little language. Failing, it leaves the cleaned prompt as it was.

rules.description: How the prompt must be written for the renderer, in words. Default: short concrete tags, subject first, no negations, no feeling words, no names.

negations.description: Words that start a negation in the game's language (default no, not, without, never): a tag that starts with one moves to the negative prompt.

judge.description: The model that rewrites the prompt; it can be a larger one than the game's judge (env IMAGES_REFINE_JUDGE_MODEL / _URL / _API win). Default: images.judge.

keepsake.description: What the person who earned it can have drawn after the game with /keepsake (needs goals.reward "keepsake").

options.description: What can be drawn: a list of phrases (may use {name}, {game}, any actor field) or "judge" to have the judge propose some that fit the setting once.

theme.description: options "judge": the setting in a sentence (default goals.theme).

safety.description: The image censor (the vision module, a host-only Python worker; needs the top-level vision block) run on pictures people attach and on every render. A flagged picture is refused (texts.unsafe) and never stored or sent; if the detector cannot run, the picture is refused too (texts.safety_down). Probabilistic, not a guarantee. Off unless this block exists.

threshold.description: Detection score from 0 to 1 at which a label blocks (default 0.5; lower is stricter).

labels.description: Image censor labels that block (default: the *_EXPOSED breast, genitalia, buttocks and anus labels). Unknown names are ignored.

uploads.description: Check attached or fetched pictures (default true).

calculated.description: Values the server works out after every change, written to game.calc.<name>. Read-only: no op and no model can write them. Use them in conditions as game.calc.<name> (a map id -> number takes an aggregate such as max or top_count).

count.description: Per actor: how many items its list field holds, e.g. actors.*.goals. With `where`, only items that match.

sum.description: One number: the total over a calculated name or a numeric actor field (actors.*.score).

min.description: One number: the lowest, same sources as sum.

max.description: One number: the highest, same sources as sum.

argmax.description: The id of the actor on top of a calculated name or numeric field; null on a tie.

argmin.description: The id of the actor at the bottom; null on a tie.

where.description: count only: keep list items whose fields equal these, e.g. {"done": true}.

at_least.description: argmax / argmin: the top value must reach this (argmax) or stay under it (argmin) to count. Default 1.

betting.description: server: code keeps chips, bets, the pot, turn order, streets and the showdown (fixed limit; blinds, ante and raise cap from game.small_blind / game.big_blind / game.ante / game.max_raises, defaults 5/10, 0, 4; side pots from game.contrib; a timed-out seat is folded by the server) and players use /check /call /raise /fold /allin; NPCs follow a fixed rule. narrator (default): the narrator keeps them. No automatic fallback. Pair with deal: server and phase writers on chips, bet, pot and status.

world.description: Where and when the story is set (era, time travel, a canon file and how anachronisms are handled).

era.description: When the story is set. custom needs canon.file.

time_travel.description: period (default): a time traveller takes on the period, bringing no items or knowledge from elsewhere. keep: they keep their own. none: there is no time travel.

file.description: A markdown file in the imeng folder (first 8000 characters) shown to the narrator as the reference for the setting.

languages.description: A character understands only the tongues in their field; speech in another is heard as sounds, not words. Off when absent.

list.description: The tongues that exist in this world.

field.description: The actor field listing the tongues that actor understands (default languages; add it to actor_template and writable_fields).

name.description: Which universe the story is in; facts from other universes do not apply.

jump.description: none (default): nobody crosses to another universe. allowed: a crossing needs a reason the game's rules give.

anachronism.description: block (default): a locked session rule, audited by the judge (needs enforce_rules); warn: the narrator reacts in character, no correction; allow: nothing.

actor_defaults_from.description: Actor field -> game field: a new actor starts with that game field's value (when it is a number) instead of the template's, e.g. {"chips": "imeng.stack"} so a table-agreed starting stack reaches players who join later.

derive.description: Game fields the server derives from other game fields after every change, e.g. {"imeng.viscosity": {from: "imeng.ambient", map: {cold: "thick", hot: "thin"}}}. The derived field is server-owned: nobody else can write it.

from.description: The game field to read, e.g. imeng.ambient.

map.description: Value of that field -> value to write.

default.description: Written when the field has no entry in the map (default empty text).

seating.description: Gated seats at a multiplayer table: /seat <age> <gender> [sexuality], then /seat yes. Only between hands (others are queued). People without a seat can watch but are not players. Off unless this block exists.

photo.description: To take a seat a person sends one checked picture of themselves.

required.description: Default true: a seat waits for a checked picture.

text_file.description: A markdown file in the imeng folder sent when someone confirms a seat: what the picture must be, that the table will see it, how long it is kept ({hours}).

keep_hours.description: Hours a seat picture is kept before it is deleted (default 24).

show.description: Default true: when the show starts the table is shown every seated person's picture (needs an images block, which serves /images).

url.description: A local HTTP service instead of the vision module: POST the picture, answer {people:[{score, keypoints:[[x,y,confidence] x 17]}]}.

threshold.description: A person counts at this score (default 0.4).

keypoint.description: A keypoint counts as visible at this confidence (default 0.5).

people.description: Most people allowed in the picture (default 1).

face_min.description: A face picture needs the image censor to find a face box at this score or higher (default off). Needs the vision module. A face under it (covered, turned, tiny) falls to the body test, else is refused.

eyes.description: A face picture needs both eyes at this confidence (default off: covered eyes are fine). With it set, a face with a covered eye falls to the body test, else is refused.

check.description: The picture check (the people come from the vision module, or check.url): exactly one person; a face (the nose shows; covered eyes or mouth are fine) or a body (both shoulders and both hips, chin to thighs). Fails closed when it cannot run. images.safety, when on, also screens every seat picture.

texts.description: rules, accepted ({kind}), format, unsafe, down, none, many, unclear, wait, shown.

start.description: When the show starts: sets game.started (server-owned), which a phase can require.

auto.description: Default true: the show starts by itself when every seat (multiplayer.max_players) is taken.

early.description: Default true: the owner may /start once multiplayer.min_players are seated.

approval.description: owner: a confirmed request waits until the table owner says /seat approve <name> (or /seat deny <name>); the owner needs no approval. Default none. Anyone may still leave at any time.

phases.description: Phases where a seat can be taken (default: between).

min_age.description: Lowest age (never below 18; game.min_age raises it per table).

fields.description: Actor fields the profile is written to (defaults age, gender, sexuality). Add them to actor_template; they are server-written, so leave them out of writable_fields.

genders.description: Allowed words for gender (default: any word).

sexualities.description: Allowed words for sexuality (default: any word).

default_sexuality.description: Used when none is given (default none).

texts.description: usage, confirm {age} {gender} {sexuality} {min}, seated {name}, queued, already, waiting, request {name} {age} {gender} {sexuality}, approved {name}, denied {name}, refused, not_owner, no_request {name}, no_owner, age {min}, gender {list}, sexuality {list}, none, full, unseated, game, welcome.

pay.description: /pay <name> <amount>: a seated real player moves a whole number of an actor field (chips) to another seated real player. Done by code, never by the narrator. Off unless this block exists.

escrow.description: Turns on /pay hold <name> <amount> (chips held by the server), /pay release (the payer pays it out, any phase) and /pay refund (back to the payer, only where payments are allowed). Held chips are paid out when a release_on phase ends.

release_on.description: Phases whose end releases every escrow to the payee (e.g. a dance phase).

texts.description: paid {from} {to} {amount}, usage, who {who}, self, poor, phase, seat, held, released, refunded, no_escrow, refund_late.

tips.description: A house tip jar (chips, never the pot): /tip any time, a cough after a few hands with no tip, a private offer to seated players. Needs betting "server" for the hand count.

amount.description: State path of one tip, a number, e.g. imeng.big_blind: /tip puts that many chips from the player's stack in the house jar (game.tips).

after_hands.description: Hands without a tip before the narrator is told to cough (default 3; a table may set game.tip_after).

on_leave.description: Also when a seated player leaves (default true).

npc_chance.description: 0 to 1: the chance an NPC that wins a hand tips (default 0).

ask.description: Sent privately to each seated real player; {amount}.

blinds.description: betting "server" only: the blinds go up like a casino's, counted in hands the server has dealt: level n multiplies the blinds the table started with (kept as game.blind_base). Fixed-limit bet sizes follow the big blind. Omit: the blinds stay as they are.

steps.description: Multipliers of the starting blinds, in order, e.g. [1, 2, 3, 5, 10]. The last stays.

audit.description: A private record of the cards for the house. Never shown to the table.

shows.description: What /audit tells the house (the owner), privately: deck (the cards set aside for the board), draws (what was turned and when), shuffles (who ran which step), hands (every player's hole cards). Default deck, draws, shuffles.

shuffle.description: Who may shuffle and whether a hand is blocked until they do.

required.description: never (default): the server shuffles by itself; each_hand: the deal waits until someone has run the ritual (game.shuffled = 1). Pair it with a phase enter_when {field: game.shuffled, gte: 1} to block the hand.

by.description: Who may /shuffle: the owner or an actor with role dealer (default), the owner or role host, any seated user, or nobody (a shuffle does nothing, like a magic deck).

ritual.description: Steps run in order as /shuffle <step>, for example ["riffle 7", "cut"]. Code does the real shuffle once it is done: the ritual is the gate.

deal.description: server: code shuffles and deals (hole cards, then the flop, turn and river from actors.table.reserve to actors.table.board) when the phase changes, and the narrator never does; narrator (default): the narrator deals. There is no automatic fallback between them. Needs phases named preflop, flop, turn and river and an actors.table.

audience.description: People without a seat as contestants: they watch, cheer and set the crowd's energy.

role.description: The actor role of people who watch (default audience).

reactions.description: energy (default): the audience's lines each round raise game.audience_energy (the crowd's mood the narrator sees); it falls when they are quiet.

decay.description: How much energy falls in a round without audience lines (default 1).

boost.description: With the crowd at or above `at`, quoted evidence of interest lifts attraction one step more than it would, never past `cap`.

at.description: Energy at which the crowd's peer pressure starts (default 6).

cap.description: The highest attraction level the crowd can lift someone to (default 2).

seats.description: The roles the owner may assign with /seat <name> <role>.

producer.description: Who may use the producer's commands.

nudge.description: Default false. Turns on /nudge <text> for the producer, in their private chat: one note for the narrator's next round, advice from someone who sees everything. The table is never told; it changes no state.

who.description: Who may use /risk, /shelter, /move and /end: the owner (default) or anyone whose actor role is `role`.

role.description: The actor role that counts as producer (default producer).

commands.description: Per-command override, for example {move: role, end: owner}.

phases.description: The steps a game goes through, gated in code (`next` entries are phase names or routes {to, ops}: ops are server operations run the moment the game arrives in `to`; `gated: true` (or {when: condition, blocks: [interrupt, idle, producer, deal, pay]}) holds the table in a phase until it moves along `next` (needs a next route; leaving is never gated); `max_rounds` (a number or a state path like imeng.dance_rounds) ends it by itself after that many turns; `private_narration` {line, recipients: "escrow", when, unless: conditions} makes the table read only `line` while the narrator reply goes to the two people named by the escrow; a phase may also have `actions` {name:{describe,allow:[paths]}} that gate what players can change and what counts as on-topic, `hook: "phases.mjs"` (a .mjs in the imeng folder exporting next({from,to,state,event}) that returns {ops, phase?}: operations applied when the game changes phase, never a replacement state), `silent: true` for a pass-through step, and `interrupt: true` to be enterable from anywhere with "@return" in its `next`): {"start":"registration","texts":{"here":"...","missing":"...","blocked":"..."},"registration":{"require":[conditions],"next":"playing","note":"words for the narrator"},"playing":{"enter_when":{},"exit_when":{},"next":["finale"]}}. game.phase only moves along `next`, when the phase being left has every `require` true and the next one has enter_when true. exit_when true: the server moves on itself.

off_phase.description: What happens to a message that matches no action of the current phase (only phases that list `actions` have one). mode: hush (default: a fixed reply picked at random from texts, no model call, nothing changes), ignore (a bare "...").

goals.description: Secret goals people write down with /goal (or in their private chat). Off unless this block exists. Needs nothing else; with phases and calculated they can gate the game.

device.description: What the game calls the private notebook (e.g. "the Notebook"). Default "notebook".

min.description: Goals each person should have (default 1). Use it in phases.require via goals_set.

max.description: Goals each person can write down (default: min, at least 1).

host.description: What the narrator is told: blind (no goals, default), own (the goals of the characters it plays: NPCs), all (everyone's).

reward.description: award (default): the tally and the reveal are the reward; points: each goal adds `points` to `score_field`; keepsake: the person who got the most goals gets a picture (needs images).

keepsake_for.description: reward "keepsake": leader (default) the person with the most goals, a tie gives nobody; done: anyone who reached at least one.

score_field.description: reward "points": the actor field that gets the points (default score).

capture_phase.description: Goals are accepted from a private note only in this phase (needs phases). Empty: any time.

npc.description: invent: an NPC with fewer than `min` goals gets one invented by the judge.

npc_after.description: Invent NPC goals from this round on (default 1).

theme.description: The setting in a sentence, so invented goals fit.

standings.description: When /goals shows how many each person reached: end (default) or always.

reveal.description: end (default): on the first round after the finale everyone's goals are told, in code.

judge.description: A different judge model for the goals (env GOALS_JUDGE_MODEL / _URL / _API win). Default: the game's judge.

texts.description: Wording of the replies and the narrator's lines (saved, full, not_here, not_now, empty, none, heading, done, open, standings, winner, tie, nobody, reveal, reaction, block, reasons, unread). {device}, {goal}, {who}, {max} are filled in.

turn_events.description: Things that happen on a game turn (needs game_turn). Ids default to ev1, ev2...

at.description: Fires the moment the game turn becomes this number.

every.description: Fires on every Nth game turn.

if.description: Only when this condition (as in exit_when; aggregates over the actors still in, e.g. top_count) is true on that turn. Not retried later.

text.description: Told to the narrator once, on the next round. With end: the closing instructions.

set.description: State changes {"game.phase": "sudden_death"} through the usual checks (allowed values, protected fields).

end.description: Close the game: the narrator writes the finale from `text`, then the game is over (wrap_up.after_text / over_reply).

turn_budget.description: Default hard: at_turn counts rounds whatever compaction does. after_compaction: at_turn and soon_turns are skipped once a recap exists (compaction is keeping the prompt small). The env CONTEXT_MAX_ROUNDS is always hard.

credits_file.description: A file in the game folder (e.g. CREDITS.md) added word for word after the narrator writes the finale. The narrator never sees or rewrites it.

evict.description: A .mjs file inside the imeng folder that decides what happens to money (debt, credit, banked) held by the people of a chat the bot was removed from. It exports evictBalances({chat, game, balances}) and returns {erase?: [userHash], log?: string}. Without it balances are kept and one line (counts and totals, no names) is logged.

credit.description: Tables only, needs the database. A busted player gets a single-use re-entry code, shown only to them; it works once paid (POST /admin/credit {paid_code}) or covered by their credit. /reentry <code>, /credit, and the owner's /lend <name> <amount>.

field.description: The actor field that is the player's stack (default chips).

empty.description: At or below this the player is busted (default 0).

game_over.description: Default true: when only one player has chips left the game is over (the ante goes back, phase registration). false: busted players stay and the game ends another way (wrap_up).

start.description: What a player comes back with, and what a code costs in credit (default 200).

debt_limit.description: The most the owner may lend one player as debt (default 0: lending is off).

code_ttl.description: How long a re-entry code works (default "7d"). The owner is told when one runs out unused.

min_antes.description: The least a player may bank, in antes (default 20): min bank = this x the ante the table registered. Banked chips are locked away from the table and from the NPC that takes a leaving player's seat.

start_from.description: A game field (e.g. imeng.stack) whose number is the re-entry stack when the table set one; start is the fallback.

currency.description: The unit of the chips (default chips): kept with every re-entry code and checked against a payment that names a currency.

require_terms.description: A payment (POST /admin/credit; the payment service is hypothetical, play chips only) must name the amount and the currency of the code, or it is refused.

max_credit.description: The most one /admin/credit call may add (default 100000).

reset.description: Game fields that go back when the game is over (the table is down to one player), besides the ante: {"imeng.small_blind": "start", "imeng.hands_played": 0}. "start" restores the value the field had when the first hand began; any other value is set as given; null removes the field.

ante.description: State path of the ante the table registered (default imeng.ante). The server records its first value as imeng.ante_start; when the table is down to one player the game is over and the ante returns to it.

frozen_borrow.description: Default false: a frozen player's character never borrows.

private_hands.description: Tables: /hand shows a player their own cards, only in their private chat. In the shared chat it refuses and points them there. The narrator must never write a hand in the shared chat (say so in the prompt).

field.description: The actor field holding a player's private cards (default hole).

hazards.description: Dangers the server rolls (hurricane, tornado, blizzard, a rare quake) that move the show to a shelter. Chance = table x season x the owner's /risk. The owner can call /shelter at once.

trigger.description: roll: the server's dice; producer: only the owner's /shelter; both (default).

phase.description: The phase in which hazards may happen (default playing).

repeat.description: Multiplier applied to every chance for each hazard that already happened (default 0.1): another one is far less likely, not impossible.

file.description: A .mjs in the imeng folder exporting hazardChance({hazard, region, lat, lon, season, base, modifier, state}) that returns the chance, or nothing to keep the table's (for example near the pole).

shelter.description: What the move to the secure shelter sets, and the line the narrator dramatises when the producer calls it.

regions.description: Values of imeng.region this can happen in; "*" means anywhere.

if.description: Only while this game field has this value (for example the place).

chance.description: Chance per round before season and the producer's /risk modifier.

seasons.description: Multipliers by imeng.season (winter, spring, summer, autumn).

sense.description: Needs betting server. Every play is weighed against the odds by code: who plays against them, and who was caught raising weak at a showdown. The narrator is told a short read; NPCs with npc_aggression use it. Off when absent.

margin.description: How far from the pot odds a play may be before it counts as against the odds (default 0.15).

window.description: How many recent decisions are kept per player (default 20).

samples.description: Boards sampled per decision to estimate the win chance (default 200; capped by the EQUITY_MAX_SAMPLES env, default 500).

bluff_below.description: A raise with a win chance under this is a bluff, not scored (default 0.3).

vision.description: The host-only Python module for seat pictures (pose) and the image censor. Models only; every rule stays in the engine. Off when absent.

python.description: The python command (default python3; with venv, the venv's own).

venv.description: A python venv folder on the host (`${NAME}` from the environment); create it with python3 -m venv and pip install -r src/tools/vision/requirements.txt.

device.description: cpu (default) or cuda; cuda runs each call inside the picture GPU lease and the worker stops after idle_stop_s.

idle_stop_s.description: Stop the worker after this many idle seconds so a GPU is returned (default 120 outside production, 0 = never in production).

timeout_s.description: How long one check may take (default 60).

pose_weights.description: A local YOLO-pose weights file (`${NAME}` allowed). Never downloaded.

url.description: A vision worker run by someone else (the same JSON over HTTP): for Docker and production.

terms.description: The game's terms, sent privately once per person.

file.description: A markdown file in the imeng folder: what the game keeps about a person and for how long, what the table can see, how to leave. Sent privately once per person and game when they are seated (seat games), join (other multiplayer games) or start (solo games). No accept step.

notice.description: The line the table sees after a seat is taken (default: The terms are in your private messages).

remember_days.description: Days before a person is sent the terms again (default 365). Remembered in the database when there is one, else in the session.

forfeit.description: A forfeit the server deals: one real player must attach a picture to a message within some rounds. Code picks them, notices the picture (it is never read by a model) and applies the penalty. Keep a database or bucket so the picture is stored and replaced by a placeholder.

chance.description: Chance (0 to 1) after each narrated round, while none is pending, that one real player is dealt a forfeit.

if.description: A per-actor condition a player must meet to be picked (e.g. not opted out).

rounds.description: Narrated rounds the player has to send a picture (default 2).

text.description: What the narrator dramatises when it is dealt. {name} is the player.

penalty.description: An actor number field changed by code when time runs out.

random_events.description: Events the server rolls after each round (chance, condition, state change, a line for the narrator). The narrator never decides whether one happens. Off unless listed.

chance.description: Chance (0 to 1) per round that the event happens while its condition holds, rolled by code.

if.description: A condition tree (see Condition trees); the event can only happen while it holds.

set.description: State changes applied when it happens, e.g. {"imeng.ambient": "hot"}.

text.description: What the narrator is told happened, to dramatise on the next round.

once.description: Default true: it can happen one time per game.

ban.description: Temporary ban from a table (multiplayer): a flagged player is put out for the hours given. The deal skips them, their messages and private channel are ignored and the narrator never hears them; they may stay on the call. Kept in the session and in the bans table when there is a database. Off unless this block exists.

wrong_guess_hours.description: The ban for the second wrong guess at another player's hidden hand in one game (default 24); the first is free.

reveal_hours.description: The ban for announcing another player's whole hidden hand correctly in a shared chat before the showdown (default 168: one week). A wrong guess costs nothing. Needs private_hands.

peek_phases.description: Phases in which /peek <name> is allowed, once per hand at one person (default ["preflop"]); anything else is a caught peek (the ban of `hours`). Needs private_hands.

flag_field.description: Actor field the narrator sets to true when the player looked at another's cards (default caught). It must be writable.

text.description: What the banned person is told; {time} is when it ends.

ruling.description: The magic-play judge: in this phase a small judge says which spell or item the player attempts and whether the character could; the narrator is told the ruling and must describe it. At a table each public line of the round is ruled on in turn. A failing judge gives no ruling. Off unless this block exists.

class_suits.description: Per class: suits that favour it (aligned) or work against it (opposed), e.g. {"wizard": {"aligned": ["spades"], "opposed": ["hearts"]}}. Added to the spell-suit alignment (aligned +1, opposed -1; the sum decides), so a card can be aligned with the spell but opposed to the class and come out neutral. Strength only.

suits.description: Spell or item name -> its suit. With deck hands, a card of that suit is aligned (strength x1.25), the other colour opposed (x0.75), the same colour neutral. Suit changes strength only, never whether it can be cast.

phase.description: The phase in which an attempt is ruled on (the Dungeon: magic).

class_field.description: Actor field holding the class (default class).

table.description: Lookup table class -> spells, owned by code: a spell not listed for the character's class is refused whatever the judge says. A class with no entry is left to the judge.

voices.description: Each NPC gets a small call of its own for what it says next (its tone fields, its private notes, the rules it set), in parallel and before the narrator, who is handed the lines as the characters' dialogue. A failing call leaves that character to the narrator. Off unless this block exists. Costs one small model call per speaking NPC per round.

feelings.description: With dating on: an NPC at or above warm_at toward someone, or at -1, is told to hint at it in its own lines. Never a number or a level; the narrator still never sees attraction. Off when absent.

warm_at.description: Attraction level from which an NPC hints at being drawn to someone (default 2).

warm.description: What the NPC is told when drawn to someone ({name}, {to}). The default is a glance, never a declaration.

cold.description: What the NPC is told when it cannot stand someone (attraction -1): mild and playful, never cruel.

roles.description: Only NPCs whose role field is one of these speak through their own call (default every named NPC).

skip.description: Actor ids that never get a voice call (default ["table"]).

naming.description: The narrator never invents a name: an NPC that arrives without one is named by a separate small call, and code checks it is clean, unused and not alike in sound or first letters to a used name; a stubborn model falls back to the code's own list. Off unless this block exists.

pool.description: Names reserved ahead of time (default 3). The narrator is told to use them, in order, for any new character it introduces, so the name is chosen by the naming call even though the narrator introduces the character. 0 turns the reserve off (names are only filled in afterwards).

prompt.description: Instruction to the naming call; {used} is the list of names already given. A default exists.

roles.description: Only actors whose role field is one of these are named (default every NPC).

skip.description: Actor ids that never get a name (default ["table"]).

deck.description: Card luck rolled by code: on every round played in this phase the server draws the top card of a shuffled deck, puts it back into the bottom half, and tells the narrator the card and its strength (2-4 half, 5-10 full, J-K 1.25, A 1.5). Off unless this block exists.

hand.description: Default 0 (one card drawn for you each round). Above 0, each player holds a hand of this many cards: the narrator shows it, the player names the card to play ("the 7 of spades"), code checks it is in the hand, plays it (it goes back into the bottom half) and deals a replacement. Naming no card in hand plays nothing yet.

phase.description: The phase in which every round draws a card.

note.description: Instruction given to the narrator with the card.

write_once.description: Actor fields that, once an op has set them, can never change again (relationship status: no breakups on live TV). The lock is kept in game.locked.

show_clock.description: A TV-format show clock in game.show_minutes: fixed costs per round, whatever the real clock says (an hour of silence costs nothing). At total the next reply is the finale. Off unless this block exists.

judge.description: Default false. A small judge reads each round for a time jump inside the story (we wait until sunrise) and adds those minutes, never more than jump_max; real-world talk (brb ten minutes) counts for nothing.

jump_max.description: Most minutes one story time jump may add (default 10).

per_round.description: Minutes a round costs when its phase has no entry in costs (default 1).

costs.description: Minutes a round costs by the phase it was played in, e.g. {"playing":3,"crossing":2}.

warn_at.description: Minute marks from which the narrator is told how long is left.

question.description: The open question gate: while game.asked names an actor, a message from anyone else does not count (nothing changes, no narrator call, they get `text`). Off unless this block exists.

field.description: Game field holding the id of the actor who was asked (default game.asked).

text.description: Reply to someone else answering; {name} is who was asked.

dating.description: The dating-show rules in code: directed attraction 0 to 3 moved by a judge's quoted evidence, one level per round; eligibility; minors never above 0. The narrator never sees game.attraction. Off unless this block exists.

status_field.description: Actor field with single, dating or married (default relationship).

age_field.description: Actor field with the real age, read by code only (default age).

contestant_role.description: Who takes part in attraction (default contestant).

npc_status.description: Odds of each relationship status for an NPC contestant, rolled once by code when notes are written (default single 0.7, dating 0.2, married 0.1). Locked once set.

finale.description: The finale result text (decided by the server; the narrator only describes it).

pair.description: What the narrator is told when two contestants pointed at each other; {a} and {b} are their names. Default crowns them King and Queen and ends the show.

none.description: What the narrator is told when nobody matched.

notes_after.description: From this round on, every NPC contestant gets private notes (likes, passions, colours, values, outfit) and discovery starts (default 2).

tone_fields.description: Actor string fields that carry a character's voice (description, outfit, address_as...). They are never masked by `pii`, and the narrator is shown them as a CHARACTER VOICE block each turn, so personality cues survive PII masking.

role_field.description: The actor field that holds a role (default "role").

field_roles.description: Which roles may have each field changed, e.g. {"warmth":["contestant"]}: an op on that field of an actor with another role is refused (the Host is never gak'd).

validate.description: A JS file in the imeng folder exporting validateOp(op, state): true, or a short reason the op is not allowed. Real functions (may use zod inside); a refused op that is valid JSON goes to the repair judge once.

repair.description: Let the judge correct a refused op once (default: on when `validate` is set, otherwise off).

judge_api.description: How the judge model is called: "ollama" (native API, default) or "openai" (an OpenAI-compatible server such as llama.cpp's llama-server; set JUDGE_URL, or it shares the narrator's server). Hosted services are not allowed.

field.description: Actor field; `game.<field>` reads a number from the shared game state.

aggregate.description: Compare the average / minimum / maximum / sum of the field over the actors still in, instead of one actor. top_count: how many of them share the highest value (2 or more is a tie at the top).

share.description: exit_group_when only, without `aggregate`: fraction (0-1, default 1) of the actors still in that must meet the comparison.

present.description: true: the field has a value (not empty, not missing); false: it has none. Works on text, lists and numbers.

is.description: The field is exactly this value (text, number or true/false).

reason.description: Words for the narrator when this is what is still missing (phases.require).
